messages:
eva: Heads-up — we need a small cross-team decision: standardizing the log <-> trace correlation fields for all services before we wire up the new OTLP pipeline. Current chaos is making the dashboard links unreliable.
lee: +1. can we just use the W3C traceparent header and derive trace_id/span_id for logs?
sam: We already get traceparent on the HTTP side, but a lot of async jobs never propagate it. Also some teams log trace_id as traceid, others as trace_id or x_trace.
nana: propose a minimal contract: logs MUST include otel.trace_id (32 hex) and otel.span_id (16 hex) when available, and service.name + env. If not present, fallback to request_id.
eva: that sounds reasonable. any concerns about breaking parsers?
mike: downstream log parsers will need a schema bump but it's small. big thing is making sure ingesters (kinesis -> logs-prod) normalize fields into "trace_id" for linking with traces in Tempo/Jaeger.
sam: question: should the field be "otel.trace_id" or just "trace_id"? our dashboards expect trace_id in the root.
lee: prefer namespaced otel.* to avoid collision in app-level JSON fields, but ingestion layer can map otel.trace_id -> trace_id for console linking.
nana: also we should publish a lint rule in CI that validates trace id format (^[0-9a-f]{32}$) and span id (^[0-9a-f]{16}$). small jest script or python check.
eva: +1 on a CI lint. ops: can we make the OTEL collector add missing trace ids for async jobs when we can reconstruct from message headers?
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: otel-collector config update to map headers -> resource attributes at 22:30 UTC :rocket:
mike: retention question: if we correlate logs -> traces, do we need longer retention for traces? currently traces are 7d, logs 30d. linking makes traces more valuable for debug history.
lee: we should keep traces 14d for critical services, rest 7d. add an annotation on traces for sampling.rate to track cost.
sam: another gotcha: sensitive payloads — ensure we don't accidentally persist PII in log->trace joins. mask at ingestion and mention in contract.
eva: action items: (1) draft a short "correlation field contract" doc with required field names and regexes; (2) add CI lint template + example; (3) otel-collector mapping PR to normalize fields and map headers; (4) ops to propose retention tiering for traces. I'll write the doc and drop a PR by EOD.
nana: I can add the lint rule and a quick integration test.
mike: ops will prototype retention tiers and cost estimate.
sam: I'll audit 10 sample services to see current field names and async propagation gaps.
eva: thanks all — ping me for reviews. :thumbsup:
lee: tiny example of recommended JSON log format:
```
{
  "timestamp": "2026-03-18T15:12:03Z",
  "level": "info",
  "message": "model request served",
  "service.name": "redwood-inference.api",
  "env": "prod",
  "otel.trace_id": "4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736",
  "otel.span_id": "00f067aa0ba902b7",
  "request_id": "r_12345"
}
```
lee: also added a snippet for the lint regex in the draft doc.
nana: noted, will make CI rule fail-fast with a link to the doc.
sam: one more thing — dashboards need a small UX tweak: when you click "view trace" from a log, if multiple traces match, show the top 3 by timestamp and span duration. avoids a noisy jump.
eva: good UX suggestion, will add that to the doc.
deploy-bot: CI:linters — all checks passed on branch correlation-docs.
lee: awesome, I'll review the PR now."
